findings.text: The alternate routing capability block is eight bytes long with a capability halfword at offset 4 and a control halfword at offset 6. The capability halfword advertises two single-bit group capabilities in its low bits and carries an eight-bit next-function number in its high byte. The control halfword provides matching enable bits in its low bits and a three-bit function-group selector taken from bits 6 down to 4.

The address translation capability block is eight bytes long with capability at offset 4 and control at offset 6. Capability carries a five-bit invalidate queue depth in its low bits, a page-aligned request flag, and an architected maximum queue depth of thirty-two. Control provides an enable flag in its top bit and a five-bit smallest translation unit field, whose minimum shift is twelve.

The page request capability uses control at offset 4, status at offset 6, a maximum supported count at offset 8 and an allowed count at offset 12, with total size sixteen bytes. Control has enable and reset flags. Status reports response failure, unexpected index, stopped, and PASID-required conditions in widely separated bits.

The process address space capability block is eight bytes with feature halfword at offset 4 and control halfword at offset 6. Feature advertises execute and privilege support plus a width field in the high byte of the halfword. Control provides enable plus matching execute and privilege enables in its low bits.

The single-root virtualization capability spans sixty-four bytes starting with capability at offset 4, control at 8 and status at 10, followed by initial, total and active virtual function counts, a dependency link, first-function offset and stride, virtual device identifier, supported and system page sizes, six base address slots from offset 36, and a migration-state table offset at 60. Control governs virtual enable, migration enable and interrupt, memory space, and alternate routing hierarchy; capability and status expose migration capability, message number, and migration status.

Virtual function migration state is a two-bit value with four ordered meanings for unavailable, migrate-in, migrate-out and available. The table pointer packs a three-bit base register selector in its low bits with the remaining high bits forming an aligned offset.

Latency tolerance reporting uses two halfword latency registers at offsets 4 and 6 plus combined encodings. Each value field is ten bits with a three-bit scale; the no-snoop combined value and scale live in the high half of a wider word with the scale shifted by ten within its subfield. Total block size is eight bytes.

Access control services use capability at offset 4, control at offset 6 and an egress vector at offset 8, with the egress vector size fixed at five. Capability and control share seven single-bit protections for source validation, translation blocking, request and completion redirect, upstream forwarding, egress control and translated peer forwarding.

The serial ATA capability encodes a register location selector at offset 4 using only its low four bits, with all-ones meaning inline in configuration space. It has two possible total sizes, a short eight-byte form and a long sixteen-byte form.

Resizable BAR capability uses capability at offset 4 and control at offset 8. Capability carries supported sizes in all but its low four bits. Control packs a three-bit BAR index, a three-bit count of resizable BARs shifted by five, and a five-bit size selector shifted by eight.
Virtual-function resizable BAR register selectors reuse exactly the physical-function capability and control offsets and masks rather than defining independent encodings.

Dynamic power allocation capability word sits at offset 4 with a five-bit substate count field encoding one less than the number of substates. The base register block without substates is sixteen bytes.

TLP hinting completeness is a two-bit value distinguishing none, hinting only, and extended hinting. The hinting capability word at offset 4 advertises three steering modes, extended requester support, a two-bit table location distinguishing absent, in-capability and in MSI-X placements, and a table size field shifted by sixteen; base size without table is twelve bytes. Control at offset 8 selects one of three steering modes and one of three requester enable levels.

Downstream port containment uses capability at offset 4, control at 6, status at 8 and source identifier at 10, followed by a root-port pending I/O log region from offset 12 through beyond 52 for status, mask, severity, system error, exception, header, implementation-specific and prefix logs. Capability advertises root extensions, poisoned completion blocking, software trigger, two-part log size, and active-link error signaling plus a message number. Control enables fatal, nonfatal and interrupt triggers.

Containment trigger status combines a triggered flag, an interrupt flag, a busy flag and a first-error pointer with a two-bit primary reason distinguishing uncorrectable, nonfatal, fatal and extended-reason cases; when extended, a further two-bit extension distinguishes pending I/O error from software trigger.

Precision time capability at offset 4 advertises requester, responder and root roles in its low bits plus an eight-bit clock granularity in its second byte. Control at offset 8 provides a global enable and a root-select flag.

L1 low-power substates use capability at 4 and two control words at 8 and 12. Capability and first control word mirror four enable or support bits for PCI power management and active-state L1.1 and L1.2 operation, including combined masks for L1.2-only and all-substate sets, alongside common-mode restore time, power-on scale and value, and latency threshold value and scale fields. The second control word carries additional power-on scale and value fields in its low byte.

Designated vendor capability headers sit at offsets 4 and 8. The first header packs a sixteen-bit vendor identifier, a four-bit revision and a twelve-bit length extracted by shifting; the second header carries a sixteen-bit identifier in its low half.

Data link feature exchange uses a capability word at offset 4 with only its top bit defined as exchange enable. Lane equalization controls use offset 12 for secondary PCI and offset 32 for 16, 32 and 64 gigatransfer physical layers; the 16 gigatransfer control further splits downstream and upstream transmitter presets into low and high nibbles with a shift of four for the upstream half.

Native enclosure management uses capability at 4, control at 8 and status at 12. Capability and control each expose a single capable or enable flag. Control also packs a reset command plus many single-bit enclosure indicators for locate, fail, rebuild, predictive failure, hot spare, array membership, device type, disabled state and eight vendor-specific slots. Status reports command completion in its low bit.

Data object exchange mailbox occupies twenty-four bytes with capability at 4, control at 8, status at 12 and write and read data ports at 16 and 20. Capability advertises interrupt support and message number. Control provides abort, interrupt enable and a top-bit go flag. Status reports busy, interrupt, error and a top-bit data-ready flag.

Data object headers encode vendor, type and length across three words: vendor in the low half of word one, type in its next byte, length in the low eighteen bits of word two, with discovery request carrying index and version bytes and discovery response carrying vendor, type and next-index bytes in defined positions.
The discovery response protocol selector is defined as identical to the discovery response type selector rather than an independent encoding.
Device 3 capability block uses capability, control and status words at offsets 4, 8 and 12. Status defines a single segment-captured flag indicating end-to-end flit mode detection.
